solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: You have to accept this seaside town's trendy

parts.note: Deal is a seaside town on the Kent coast in south-east England; the 's stands for 'is', joining it to what follows
with it is an old slang phrase for fashionable or up to date

explanation.surface: A tourist remarks that a certain seaside resort has become rather fashionable.
explanation.walkthrough: DEAL is a town on the Kent coast in England.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a blunt instruction to put up with something unwelcome, matching 'you have to accept this'.

clue.text: Song's no good — awful

indicators.note: the song has no good, so that letter is dropped from it

parts.note: a dirge is a mournful song; the 's stands for 'has'

explanation.surface: A music critic dismisses a track as no good and simply awful.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'Song's no good' as 'the song has no G': take G from DIRGE.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: something dreadful or terrible can be called awful.

clue.text: Crushing hug is an agonising thing

indicators.note: crushing squashes these letters out of shape into a new order

explanation.surface: A bear hug so tight it becomes painful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crushing' describes the hug in the surface but signals the rearrangement of HUG IS AN.
explanation.definitionFit: Severe mental or physical suffering is an agonising experience, a noun to match 'thing'.

clue.text: I let His Excellency pawn the bizarre unwanted gift

indicators.note: bizarre means weird, so these letters come out in a strange new order

parts.note: HE is the usual abbreviation for His Excellency, an ambassador's title

explanation.surface: An ambassador is allowed to hock an odd present he never wanted.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: a burdensome possession nobody wants, from the legend of Siamese kings giving costly sacred animals to rivals.

clue.text: Agreement to have food during test

indicators.note: the eating happens during the test, so one word sits within the other

parts.note: to try something is to test it
to eat is to have food

explanation.surface: Someone is allowed to eat in the middle of an exam.
explanation.definitionFit: A formal pact between nations is an agreement.

clue.text: Scientists taking time to bisect livid bug

indicators.note: to bisect is to cut in two, so these letters split the angry word

parts.note: livid means very angry, irate

indicators.note: the scientists take time along with them, one beside the other

parts.note: RI is the Royal Institution, a British scientific body

explanation.surface: Researchers take time to slice an angry insect in half.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bug' looks like an insect but is a verb; 'to bisect' splits the angry word in two around the scientists and time.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb, to bug someone is to annoy them.

clue.text: Song of one cast out after taking sides

indicators.note: the sides, or outer letters, are taken away

parts.note: a pariah is an outcast shunned by society

explanation.surface: A ballad about an outcast who chose a side in a dispute.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Taking sides' suggests joining a faction; here it removes PARIAH's outer letters P and H.
explanation.definitionFit: An operatic solo for one voice is a kind of song.

clue.text: Bring website up to date about attempt to silence whistle-blower previously

indicators.note: the referee comes earlier than the rest

parts.note: a referee blows a whistle in a match
re means about or concerning
sh is said to hush someone

explanation.surface: A company updates its website after trying to gag an employee who leaked secrets.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Whistle-blower' suggests an informant, but it is a match official.
explanation.definitionFit: To reload a web page shows its latest content, bringing it up to date.

clue.text: A b-brood heartlessly consumed, as prowling predator will?

indicators.note: without its heart, the single central letter is removed

parts.note: the stammered b-b signals a stutter, so a brood (a litter) is said with its first letter twice
ate means consumed

explanation.surface: A predator heartlessly devours a stammered-over brood of young.
explanation.walkthrough: LITTER stuttered gives LLITTER; its central T goes. 'Prowling predator' repeats a P sound, as the answer does.
explanation.definitionFit: Words starting with the same sound, like prowling and predator, repeat that sound in sequence.

clue.text: Kind of music newspaper/magazine

parts.note: a rag is a disparaging word for a newspaper
Time is a well-known American news magazine

explanation.surface: A publication described as both newspaper and magazine.
explanation.definitionFit: Syncopated piano style popular around 1900, an example of a kind of music.

clue.text: In a flap, fluster, needing to get calm

indicators.note: being in a flap means agitated, so the letters are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: Someone agitated and flustered needs to settle down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In a flap' and 'fluster' both seem part of the panic; the first signals rearranging the second.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: something peaceful and soothing is calm.

clue.text: Put down the receiver and remain neutral

definitions.meaning: read as suppressing a dealer in stolen goods (a fence), rather than hanging up a phone
to refuse to take either side in a dispute

explanation.surface: Hang up the phone and stay out of the argument.
explanation.walkthrough: A fence is someone who receives stolen goods; to sit on someone is to squash them.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: avoiding commitment to either side, like perching astride a boundary.

clue.text: Dress fitted the tiny character being taken on illegally

indicators.note: to dress is to arrange, as troops dress their ranks, so the letters are set in a new order

explanation.surface: A small person is fitted for a dress, perhaps unlawfully.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dress' looks like a garment but is a verb meaning arrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Fraudsters who assume another person's persona commit this crime, a cryptic gloss on taking on a character.

clue.text: In endless outing drinking pints, hack'll write this …

indicators.note: drinking takes the beer inside
without its end, the final letter goes

parts.note: a journey is a trip or outing
pints are typically of ale, so pints stands for ales

explanation.surface: A reporter on an interminable trip, drinking pints, will write in this style.
explanation.walkthrough: JOURNEY loses its last letter Y and then takes in ALES. A hack is a journalist.
explanation.definitionFit: Hackneyed, cliché-ridden newspaper prose is the style a hack writes in.

clue.text: Having short break, daughter's awaiting connection

parts.note: on, as in on holiday, means having or taking a break
hol is a short form of holiday
D is an abbreviation for daughter; the 's stands for 'is'

explanation.surface: A daughter on a brief holiday is waiting for her flight connection.
explanation.definitionFit: A phone caller left waiting to be put through is in this state.

clue.text: A ship, reportedly stationary?

indicators.note: reportedly means as heard, so a phrase is swapped for one sounding the same

parts.note: a tanker is a ship carrying liquid cargo

explanation.surface: A news item says a vessel is not moving.
explanation.definitionFit: A moored vessel held by its heavy hook is not moving, hence stationary.

clue.text: … with account in boozer that's example of black-and-white issue?

indicators.note: the two pieces sit in the pub

parts.note: a boozer is British slang for a pub
and means together with

explanation.surface: A drinker settles an account in the pub over a black-and-white matter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Issue' means offspring, and a giant panda is black and white.
explanation.definitionFit: A young giant panda is offspring of a black-and-white animal.

clue.text: Pick fruit for show again

parts.note: to reap is to gather a crop
a pear is a fruit

explanation.surface: Picking fruit to enter at a show again.
explanation.definitionFit: To show up once more is to come into view a second time.

clue.text: Adjusted treadle after shift?

indicators.note: after being shifted around, the letters stand in a new order

explanation.surface: A sewing machine's foot pedal adjusted following a work shift.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: something modified or changed has been adjusted.

clue.text: Property cleaner mainly rented

indicators.note: mainly means most of it, so the last letter goes

parts.note: a char is a British cleaning woman
let means rented out

explanation.surface: A house mostly let to a cleaner.
explanation.walkthrough: A char (charwoman) is an old British word for a cleaner.
explanation.definitionFit: An Alpine-style wooden house is an example of a property.

clue.text: Indian spinach filling in lean minced meat dish

indicators.note: filling in means occupying the inside
minced means chopped up, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: sag is the Indian word for spinach, as in sag aloo

explanation.surface: A recipe with spinach mixed into lean minced meat.
explanation.walkthrough: LEAN rearranged gives LANE, which SAG fills.
explanation.definitionFit: Italian baked pasta layered with minced meat sauce is a meat dish.

clue.text: Aware of press release having precedence with dispatch

indicators.note: having precedence means coming first

parts.note: PR is public relations, the work of issuing press releases
to be onto something is to be aware of it

explanation.surface: Someone who knows that a press release takes priority sends it out quickly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dispatch' looks like sending something out; here it means speed.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: doing something promptly or quickly is acting with dispatch.

clue.text: Painting dune-buggies, perhaps, in turn-of-the-century style

parts.note: painting is a form of art
dune-buggies are vehicles for sand, so playfully sand crafts

explanation.surface: Painting beach buggies in a decorative period style.
explanation.definitionFit: The decorative design movement of around 1900, led by William Morris, is a style from that period.

clue.text: Courier emitting zero? That might make him green

indicators.note: emitting means giving out, so the letter leaves

parts.note: an envoy is a messenger or courier
O looks like zero

explanation.surface: A messenger giving off nothing turns green.
explanation.definitionFit: Jealousy is called the green-eyed monster, so this feeling makes someone green.

clue.text: Wandering rodent nesting in Morecambe?

indicators.note: nesting in means lodged inside

parts.note: Eric Morecambe was a much-loved British comedian
a rat is a rodent

explanation.surface: A rat found living in the seaside town of Morecambe.
explanation.walkthrough: Morecambe is a Lancashire resort, but here it is the comedian Eric Morecambe, of Morecambe and Wise.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: something irregular and straying from a course is wandering.

clue.text: I refuse horse at agreed figure

parts.note: no is a refusal
a nag is an old horse
on means agreed, as in 'the deal is on'

explanation.surface: A jumper refuses a fence at an agreed figure, like a horse balking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Refuse' suggests a horse balking at a jump; it is a plain no.
explanation.definitionFit: A nine-sided polygon is a geometrical figure.

clue.text: Bring west strange eastern vegetable

indicators.note: in an across clue, bringing west means reading right to left

parts.note: odd means strange

explanation.surface: Import an unusual vegetable from the east.
explanation.definitionFit: A taro root eaten in tropical cooking is an example of a vegetable.

clue.text: Old student alone with screen losing focus, in an old-fashioned way

parts.note: OB is an old boy, a former pupil
sole means alone, only

indicators.note: losing its focus means losing its central letter

parts.note: telly is British slang for television

explanation.surface: A former student alone with a blurred television screen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Losing focus' suggests blurring; it removes one middle L from TELLY.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: something outdated is done in an old-fashioned way.
